scenario_name: Legacy Cancellation Update After Backfill Batch

traces.hypothesis: The backfill process reads a row state before a legacy update occurs, but the legacy update only modifies the legacy column, leaving the new column stale because no synchronization mechanism exists.

step_outcomes.sql_executed: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS order_statuses (id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(32) UNIQUE NOT NULL); INSERT INTO order_statuses (id, name) VALUES (1, 'pending'), (2, 'paid'), (3, 'shipped'), (4, 'refunded') ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING; ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS status_id INT REFERENCES order_statuses(id);
UPDATE orders o SET status_id = s.id FROM order_statuses s WHERE o.status = s.name AND o.status_id IS NULL;
UPDATE orders SET status = 'refunded' WHERE id = 42;

invariant_results.sql_query: SELECT o.id, o.status AS legacy_status, o.status_id, os.name AS lookup_status FROM orders o JOIN order_statuses os ON o.status_id = os.id WHERE o.status != os.name;

tool_output.scenario_name: Legacy Cancellation Update After Backfill Batch
tool_output.description: A legacy cancellation updates only the text status to refunded after that row has already been processed by the backfill. The new status_id identifier remains stale as pending.
